title: John Chapter 20 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 20 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 20 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who came to the sepulchre early on the first day of the week?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene is mentioned as the one who came to the sepulchre early on the first day of the week in John 20:1.

questions.question: What did Mary Magdalene see at the sepulchre?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene saw that the stone had been taken away from the sepulchre in John 20:1.

questions.question: To whom did Mary Magdalene report the absence of Jesus?
options: Simon Peter and the other disciple whom Jesus loved
questions.correctAnswer: Simon Peter and the other disciple whom Jesus loved
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple to inform them that the Lord was taken away from the sepulchre in John 20:2.

questions.question: Which disciple outran Peter to the sepulchre?
questions.explanation: The other disciple, who is traditionally understood to be John, outran Peter and came first to the sepulchre as stated in John 20:4.

questions.question: What did John see when he looked into the sepulchre?
questions.explanation: John saw the linen clothes lying in the sepulchre when he looked in, according to John 20:5.

questions.question: True or False: Mary Magdalene wept outside the sepulchre.
questions.explanation: Mary stood without at the sepulchre weeping, as stated in John 20:11.

questions.question: What did Mary see inside the sepulchre after looking in while she was weeping?
questions.explanation: Mary saw two angels in white sitting where the body of Jesus had lain, as stated in John 20:12.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples immediately understood that Jesus must rise again from the dead.
questions.explanation: They did not yet know the scripture that he must rise again from the dead, as stated in John 20:9.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to Mary when she did not recognize Him?
questions.explanation: Jesus called Mary by name, saying 'Mary' which led her to recognize Him, as stated in John 20:16.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus instructed Mary to touch Him.
questions.explanation: Jesus told Mary not to touch Him because He had not yet ascended to His Father, as stated in John 20:17.

questions.question: In what condition were the doors when Jesus appeared to the disciples?
questions.explanation: The doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews when Jesus came, according to John 20:19.

questions.question: What did Jesus show to His disciples when He appeared to them?
questions.explanation: Jesus showed His hands and His side to the disciples, which made them glad, as stated in John 20:20.

questions.question: True or False: Thomas was present when Jesus first appeared to the disciples.
questions.explanation: Thomas was not with the disciples when Jesus came the first time, as stated in John 20:24.

questions.question: What command did Jesus give regarding the Holy Ghost?
questions.explanation: Jesus breathed on them and said, 'Receive ye the Holy Ghost,' as stated in John 20:22.

questions.question: What comes first in John 20?
options: Mary tells the disciples about Jesus
questions.explanation: The first event in John 20 is Mary Magdalene arriving at the sepulchre early on the first day of the week, according to John 20:1.

medium.title: John Chapter 20 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 20 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Mary Magdalene see when she arrived at the sepulchre?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene saw the stone taken away from the sepulchre when she arrived there, as stated in John 20:1.

questions.question: Who did Mary Magdalene inform about the missing body of Jesus?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene ran to Simon Peter and the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, to tell them that the Lord was taken away, as mentioned in John 20:2.

questions.question: What significant action did the other disciple do before Peter when they reached the sepulchre?
questions.explanation: The other disciple outran Peter and came first to the sepulchre, as noted in John 20:4.

questions.question: What did Peter find when he entered the sepulchre?
questions.explanation: When Peter entered the sepulchre, he saw the linen clothes lie, as described in John 20:6.

questions.question: What did the angels ask Mary Magdalene?
questions.explanation: The angels asked Mary why she was weeping, as recorded in John 20:13.

questions.question: What did Mary Magdalene initially think when she saw Jesus after she turned around?
questions.explanation: Mary thought Jesus was the gardener when she first saw him and did not recognize him, according to John 20:15.

questions.question: What message did Jesus give to Mary Magdalene regarding his ascension?
options: To tell the disciples he is ascending
questions.correctAnswer: To tell the disciples he is ascending
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed Mary to go to his brethren and tell them he is ascending to the Father, as stated in John 20:17.

questions.question: What did Jesus show the disciples to prove his identity?
questions.explanation: Jesus showed his hands and his side to the disciples to prove he was alive, as recorded in John 20:20.

questions.question: What did Jesus breathe on the disciples and say to them?
questions.explanation: Jesus breathed on them and said to receive the Holy Ghost, as indicated in John 20:22.

questions.question: Did Thomas believe the other disciples when they told him they had seen the Lord?
questions.explanation: Thomas did not believe the other disciples' claim of seeing the Lord unless he saw the marks of the nails and put his hand into Jesus' side, as per John 20:25.

questions.question: When Jesus appeared to the disciples a week later, what did he say to them?
questions.explanation: When Jesus appeared to the disciples a week later, he greeted them with 'Peace be unto you,' as found in John 20:26.

questions.question: Did Jesus commend Thomas for needing to see him in order to believe?
questions.explanation: Jesus told Thomas that those who have not seen and yet have believed are blessed, indicating that he did not commend Thomas for needing physical evidence, as seen in John 20:29.

hard.title: John Chapter 20 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 20.

questions.question: Who was the first to see the sepulchre with the stone taken away?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene is mentioned as the first to come to the sepulchre and see the stone taken away in John 20:1.

questions.question: What did Mary Magdalene tell Simon Peter and the other disciple?
options: They have taken away the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: They have taken away the Lord
questions.explanation: Mary told them that they have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, as stated in John 20:2.

questions.question: What did the other disciple do when he reached the sepulchre?
options: He stooped down and looked in
questions.correctAnswer: He stooped down and looked in
questions.explanation: The other disciple, upon reaching the sepulchre, stooped down and looked in but did not enter, as mentioned in John 20:5.

questions.question: What did Peter see when he entered the sepulchre?
questions.explanation: Peter saw the linen clothes lying in the sepulchre after he entered, as stated in John 20:6.

questions.question: What was distinct about the napkin found in the sepulchre?
options: It was folded and set apart
It was found in Mary's possession
questions.correctAnswer: It was folded and set apart
questions.explanation: The napkin was not lying with the linen clothes but was wrapped together in a place by itself, as mentioned in John 20:7.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to Mary when he appeared to her?
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed Mary not to touch him because he had not yet ascended to the Father, as stated in John 20:17.

questions.question: What did Jesus show to his disciples to prove his resurrection?
questions.explanation: Jesus showed his hands and side to the disciples to prove that it was him, as mentioned in John 20:20.

questions.question: What did Jesus breathe on the disciples, saying they should receive it?
questions.explanation: Jesus breathed on them and said to receive the Holy Ghost, as indicated in John 20:22.

questions.question: What was Thomas's condition during Jesus's first appearance to the disciples?
questions.explanation: Thomas was not with the disciples when Jesus first came to them, as stated in John 20:24.

questions.question: What did Thomas insist on before he would believe in the resurrection?
options: He wanted to hear the angels
He wanted to see Jesus's face
He wanted to touch Jesus's wounds
He wanted to see the empty tomb
questions.correctAnswer: He wanted to touch Jesus's wounds
questions.explanation: Thomas insisted that he would not believe unless he could see and touch the print of the nails and Jesus's side, as indicated in John 20:25.

questions.question: What does Jesus say about those who have not seen and yet have believed?
questions.explanation: Jesus declares that those who have not seen and yet have believed are blessed, as stated in John 20:29.

questions.question: True or False: Mary Magdalene was the first to see the risen Lord.
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene was indeed the first to see the risen Lord, as she encountered Jesus after the resurrection, as indicated in John 20:14.

questions.question: True or False: The Gospel of John ends with the resurrection of Jesus.
questions.explanation: The Gospel of John does not end with the resurrection; it concludes with a statement about the signs of Jesus, as found in John 20:30-31.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophecy is echoed in Jesus's command to the disciples about forgiving sins?
questions.explanation: Jesus's command to remit sins connects to the promise of the new covenant in Ezekiel 36:27, where God promises to put His Spirit in them, enabling them to follow His decrees.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Greek word 'pneuma' used in reference to the Holy Spirit?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'pneuma' translates to 'breath' or 'spirit', which indicates the life-giving aspect of the Holy Spirit that Jesus breathed on his disciples, as seen in John 20:22.

theological.title: John Chapter 20 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 20 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does John 20:9 reveal about the disciples' understanding of Jesus' resurrection?
options: They believed He would rise again
They were unaware of the scripture
They thought He was still dead
questions.correctAnswer: They were unaware of the scripture
questions.explanation: John 20:9 states, 'For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead,' indicating their lack of understanding regarding the necessity of His resurrection.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by Jesus' ability to appear in a locked room in John 20:19?
questions.explanation: Jesus' sudden appearance among His disciples in a locked room illustrates His omnipresence, as He transcends physical barriers, showing He is not limited by space as humans are.

questions.question: What does the interaction between Jesus and Mary in John 20:16 reveal about His identity?
options: He is the Son of God
questions.explanation: In John 20:16, when Jesus calls Mary by name and she responds, 'Rabboni; which is to say, Master,' it affirms His role as her teacher and spiritual leader.

questions.question: How does the resurrection event in John 20 contribute to the doctrine of salvation?
options: It shows the resurrection is optional
It confirms Jesus as a teacher
It affirms Jesus as the source of eternal life
It proves Jesus was a martyr
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms Jesus as the source of eternal life
questions.explanation: The resurrection is central to the Christian faith as it validates Jesus' claims about Himself and His power over death, providing believers with the hope of eternal life (see John 11:25).

questions.question: What significance does the linen clothes in the sepulchre have according to John 20:5?
options: They were left behind by the gardener
They prove the tomb was empty
questions.explanation: The presence of the linen clothes lying in the tomb suggests that Jesus' resurrection was not a mere resuscitation but a transformation, as He left the burial garments behind (John 20:5).

questions.question: What does John 20:22 imply about the role of the Holy Spirit in the life of the disciples?
options: They were to rely on their wisdom
They were to wait for Pentecost
questions.explanation: In John 20:22, when Jesus breathed on them and said, 'Receive ye the Holy Ghost,' it signifies the impartation of divine power needed for their mission to preach the Gospel (Acts 1:8).

questions.question: What lesson can be drawn from the disciples' response to Mary's report in John 20:18?
options: They doubted and did not respond
questions.correctAnswer: They doubted and did not respond
questions.explanation: The disciples did not initially believe Mary Magdalene's testimony about seeing the Lord, highlighting a theme of doubt and the gradual realization of Jesus' resurrection (John 20:18).

questions.question: How does Jesus’ statement to Thomas in John 20:27 connect to the theme of faith?
options: Faith is rooted in unseen truths
Doubt is acceptable for all believers
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is rooted in unseen truths
questions.explanation: In John 20:27, Jesus encourages Thomas to believe without having to see, emphasizing that true faith often exists without physical evidence, as indicated in Hebrews 11:1.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth is underscored by John 20:31 regarding the purpose of the Gospel of John?
options: To reveal the history of the Jews
To provide evidence of Jesus’ miracles
To affirm Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God
To list the teachings of Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: To affirm Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God
questions.explanation: John 20:31 explicitly states that the purpose of the Gospel is to affirm that Jesus is the Christ, helping believers understand His divine identity and the salvation He offers.

questions.question: What theological significance does the appearance of angels in John 20:12 hold?
options: They indicate the divine approval of Jesus
They serve as witnesses to the resurrection
They remind people of the law
questions.correctAnswer: They serve as witnesses to the resurrection
questions.explanation: The presence of angels in John 20:12, positioned at the head and feet where Jesus lay, serves as heavenly witnesses to His resurrection and validates the event's importance.

questions.question: What is the significance of Jesus calling Mary by name in John 20:16?
options: It shows His familiarity with her
questions.correctAnswer: It shows His familiarity with her
questions.explanation: When Jesus calls Mary by name, it reflects His personal relationship with her, illustrating how He knows and cares for His followers (John 20:16).

questions.question: What does John 20:23 teach about the authority given to the disciples?
questions.explanation: In John 20:23, Jesus grants the disciples authority to remit or retain sins, indicating a significant role in the establishment of the church's authority and mission (Matthew 16:19).

questions.question: According to John 20:24-25, what was Thomas's initial stance regarding Jesus' resurrection?
options: He was skeptical and demanded proof
questions.correctAnswer: He was skeptical and demanded proof
questions.explanation: Thomas expressed skepticism about Jesus' resurrection, stating that he would not believe unless he saw the physical evidence, highlighting the challenge of faith (John 20:24-25).

questions.question: What does the repeated greeting of 'Peace be unto you' in John 20:19 and 21 signify?
questions.explanation: By saying 'Peace be unto you,' Jesus reassures His disciples of His presence and the reconciliation that His resurrection brings, emphasizing the peace that comes from Him (John 20:19, 21).

questions.question: How does John 20 connect to the broader narrative of redemption in Scripture?
options: It shows the end of Jesus' ministry
It affirms the fulfillment of prophecy
It highlights the resurrection as central to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights the resurrection as central to salvation
questions.explanation: John 20 is pivotal in the redemptive narrative, as it confirms the resurrection of Christ, which is foundational for the Christian faith and the assurance of salvation (1 Corinthians 15:17).
